facts.text: The project is a Gymnasium environment for Super Mario Bros., Super Mario Bros. 2 (Lost Levels), Super Mario Bros. 2 (USA) and Super Mario Bros. 3 on the NES, running through the nes-py emulator
By default the environments use the full NES action space of 256 discrete actions
The legal reward range is -15 to 15
A step's reward is the sum of the progress, time, score, coins, powerup, completion and death components; the info dictionary also reports the unclipped and the clipped total
The death reward component is -25 while Mario is dying or dead
The completion reward component is 50, paid once when the flag is reached
The game is over when the life counter is 0xff (255), the value it holds when no lives are left
A full-game environment terminates on game over; a single-stage environment also terminates on dying, dead or flag reached

The info dictionary reports area, coins, enemy types, flag_get, is_dead, is_dying, is_game_over, is_stage_over, is_world_over, left_x_pos, level, life, player_state, powerup_level, score, stage, status, status_value, time, world, x_pos, x_pos_max, y_pixel, y_pos and y_viewport
A reset returns a two-item tuple and a step returns a five-item tuple (observation, reward, terminated, truncated, info)
The documented 1-1 opening info has 0 coins, 2 lives, world 1, score 0, stage 1, time 400 and x_pos 40
The registered time limit is 9999999 steps
SuperMarioBros-v0 is registered as a Super Mario Bros. environment
The registered entry point is gym_super_mario_bros:SuperMarioBrosEnv and the environment is marked nondeterministic
A target world is 1 to 8 (1 to 13 for Lost Levels) and a target stage is 1 to 4

determinism.notes: reset(seed) or cap.world.seed.v1 fixes the fake's starting offset and the fake then advances deterministically; upstream registers nondeterministic=True (_registration.py:41), so the upstream emulator's own random number generator is not claimed to follow this seed

gaps: no dynamics are claimed (F0): the fake assigns positions and state transitions directly and does not integrate forces or contacts
the pinned clone does not state a frame duration; one step advances one NES frame, and timestep_ms is 0 because the emulator's frame rate lives outside this clone

the fake is a compact stand-in for the NES/nes-py emulator, not the emulator: it models the reset/step interface, the 256-action space, a monotone horizontal position and the in-game clock, not the game rules, collisions, enemies or level geometry

the real observation is the emulator's NES screen, a uint8 array of shape 240 x 256 x 3 (nes-py _native.pyx:21-22,31 and nes_env.py:61-65 at commit 8d27b099f24a57afaac7339fab7ec0f1f96a59c8); the fake returns a 2 x 2 x 3 uint8 stand-in of the same type and rank
no wall-clock pacing and no rendering: realtime_factor 0 and the fake has no render()
no physical device is modelled and the model was never validated against one
snapshot and restore are not offered: the bridge requires get_state/set_state, which the upstream class does not expose (the emulator's own save_state/load_state is not that interface)

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: a step or reset is refused once the runtime's e-stop latch is engaged; the world state is kept and stays readable, and the latch is cleared only by mhs.safety.reset
